title: Grade 8 Science — Tue, Jun 10
description: Metals and Non-metals — Day 2 of 5: Chemical properties
subject: science

questions.question: When metals react with oxygen, they form:
questions.explanation: Metals burn or react with oxygen to form metal oxides (e.g., 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO — magnesium oxide).

questions.question: Metal oxides are generally:
questions.explanation: Metal oxides are basic in nature. For example, CaO (lime) and MgO dissolve in water to form alkaline solutions.

questions.question: Non-metal oxides are generally:
questions.explanation: Non-metal oxides are acidic. CO₂ dissolves in water to form carbonic acid; SO₂ forms sulphurous acid.

questions.question: When sodium metal is placed in water, it reacts vigorously to produce:
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂↑. Sodium reacts violently with water, producing sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas.

questions.question: Which gas is released when a metal reacts with dilute acid?
questions.explanation: Metals react with dilute acids to produce a metal salt and hydrogen gas. E.g., Fe + H₂SO₄ → FeSO₄ + H₂↑.

questions.question: Which metal does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper is a less reactive metal and does not react with dilute HCl. Gold and silver also do not react with dilute acids.

questions.question: Iron rusts when it reacts with oxygen and ____ together.
questions.explanation: Rusting of iron (corrosion) requires both oxygen and water (moisture). The chemical name for rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide.

questions.question: Aluminium does not corrode easily even though it is a reactive metal because:
options: It forms a thin, protective layer of aluminium oxide on its surface
It does not react with oxygen
questions.explanation: Aluminium reacts quickly with oxygen to form a thin, tough layer of Al₂O₃ on its surface, which prevents further corrosion.

questions.question: Non-metals generally do NOT react with water. Which non-metal is an exception that reacts violently with water?
questions.explanation: Fluorine is highly reactive and reacts vigorously with water. Most non-metals like carbon and sulphur do not react with water.

questions.question: The reaction of acid with a metal oxide (base) to form salt and water is called:
questions.explanation: Neutralisation: acid + metal oxide (base) → salt + water. E.g., HCl + CaO → CaCl₂ + H₂O.

questions.question: When magnesium ribbon burns in air, the ash produced is:
questions.explanation: Magnesium burns with a bright white flame and forms white magnesium oxide (MgO) ash.

questions.question: Which of these is an acidic non-metal oxide?
questions.explanation: SO₂ (sulphur dioxide) is a non-metal oxide. It dissolves in water to form sulphurous acid (H₂SO₃) — an acid.

questions.question: Gold and silver are called noble metals because they:
options: Do not react with oxygen, water, or dilute acids easily
questions.explanation: Gold and silver are noble (inert) metals — they resist corrosion and do not react with oxygen, water, or dilute acids.

questions.question: Sulphur reacts with oxygen when heated to produce:
questions.explanation: S + O₂ → SO₂. Sulphur burns in oxygen to produce sulphur dioxide, a choking, acidic gas.

questions.question: When zinc reacts with dilute sulphuric acid, the products are:
questions.explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑. Zinc displaces hydrogen from sulphuric acid to form zinc sulphate and hydrogen gas.
